body: I suspect you are suffering from db inconsistencies for some reasons, one possibility being the one fixed in #6239 recently. Unfortunately that fix isn't out in any release yet and won't be for about a week (1.4.0-rc.1 on the 11th). If you're willing, I'd like to look at the databases in question ("index-0.14.0.db" in the config dirs), especially given the last folder which is "in sync" yet mismatching. If you could zip those up and put them somewhere on the internet, privately if you like (my email is  in my profile and ... everywhere).

Thanks, I will consider this.
In the meantime I attempted to manually "fix" the problem by moving the files (mentioned in the out of sync list) on device A out of the folder and back. This triggered re-sync and now device A shows that it's "Up to Date" with device B.

However, the folder X still has different sizes on the devices. And I still see this.

Device A:
![изображение](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6467552/73633660-d1115e00-4691-11ea-9b71-26eba245b854.png)

Device B:
![изображение](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6467552/73633676-de2e4d00-4691-11ea-8b57-2224f7f8421c.png)

> I'd like to look at the databases in question ("index-0.14.0.db" in the config dirs), especially given the last folder which is "in sync" yet mismatching. If you could zip those up and put them somewhere on the internet, privately if you like (my email is in my profile and ... everywhere).

Sent via email. Thank you.

Thanks for the indexes. Looking at those there's a systematic problem of missing sequence entries. 

A (Windows):

```
% stindex -mode idxck index-v0.14.0.db.windows
Sequence entry missing for FileInfo "...", folder "jxxmg-demss", seq 2794
...
Folder 6 missing 15 sequence entries: #2790 - #2804
Folder 6 missing 2 sequence entries: #2806 - #2807
Folder 6 missing 4 sequence entries: #2812 - #2815
Folder 6 missing 2 sequence entries: #2819 - #2820
```

The entries are for normal files (non-deleted, non-invalid, etc.) that each look fine.


B (Linux):

```
Sequence entry missing for FileInfo "...", folder "qp3zu-wkpkj", seq 76
Folder 6 missing 4 sequence entries: #6 - #9
Folder 6 missing 70 sequence entries: #12 - #81
```

The entries in this case are for directories.

So something is causing us to either not flush sequence entries to disk or the database forgets them after the fact. This needs looking at.

Seems likely or at least possible that the missing ranges correspond to one commit batch each.

rename.to: Syncing issues, database missing sequence entries

body: Frankly I don't see how this could happen without the bug being somewhere in the database I/O itself. When updating files we iterate over the files, and for each file write the new entries and sequences and potentially flush the batch to disk. It's not like we first write the file entries in a batch and only then the sequences. The only thing that sets the sequences apart from the other entries is that they have a higher prefix so when compacted they all get stuffed into a higher numbered file than the file entries...

I am happy to do more testing and/or provide more information if needed.
My only observation so far is that the issues happened on relatively big folders with thousands of files. Smaller folders got synced fine.

Not sure if this helps, but also:
1. After adding the folder X and starting the sync I noticed that some files were not needed so I deleted them from device A during the sync. I guess this is a normal situation, but still I kind of interfered.
2. I also noticed another minor bug with another folder that I synced with my phone. So on the phone I enabled sync with devices A and B and then in web UI of both A and B I checked this folder to be shared between these devices. Later, when I ran into the issues described above I thought that it could be somehow related (because device A also showed these files in the "out of sync" list), so I decided to uncheck the sync of this folder between devices A and B. However, after I unchecked it and clicked "Save" I noticed that the files were still in that list, and when I reopened the sharing dialog for that folder on A or B (don't remember exactly) it was still on like if I haven't disabled it (it was still checked). I repeated that a number of times until it finally got disabled and the files disappeared from "out of sync" list.
This is most likely unrelated, but I'm just reporting as much as I can :-)
I suspect unrelated on both counts. Trying reproduce via stress test but no luck on that so far unfortunately.

issue.title: Device name and other fields not shown in "New Device" message

labels.name: frozen-due-to-age
labels.description: Issues closed and untouched for a long time, together with being locked for discussion

issue.body:
In #6304 I reported a part of my current configuration.

In the UI of device B which runs on Debian the UI shows the "New Device" messages like this:

![изображение](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6467552/73659440-d938c000-46c8-11ea-86c1-de08833839b8.png)

As far as I remember it displayed the full info previously but at some point started to show it like this. On other devices this issue doesn't occur.

body:
So the problem continues.
With folder X I decided to re-share it with another remote device C, which already has this folder in a more up-to-date state (I synced it before with device A using Resilio and then added some new files to it).
My overall goal was to keep devices A and C in sync using B as a kind of a proxy.
So I had to delete folder X from A and B in Syncthing UI (otherwise it created duplicate folders - I'm not sure how this should be managed in Syncthing - if I already have a folder on A and B in sync and C has the more recent version of this folder - how do I put them all in sync?).
Then I shared this folder from device C with both A and B.

The results are:
1. Some re-sanning happened on A and B.
2. Nothing seems to have changed in terms of the files on A and B - they are not synced with C and also still out of sync with each other. And nothing is syncing.
3. C currently shows it's syncing with A and B - both in "Folders" and "Remote Devices" sections.
4. A and B currently show the folder as "Up to Date", but in "Remote Devices" they show "syncing" with C. A also shows that it's syncing with B.

Is there some workaround to fix this? I really wanted to switch to Syncthing and I'm okay to do some manual fixes, but I need this data in sync to keep working on my projects.

Device C is similar to device A - runs the latest Syncthing on Windows 7.

Regarding different sizes of folders - I think I found the reason.
The thing is - on Debian I was checking the size in Midnight Commander (mc), and it seems that it has some inconsistency in its size calculations.

UPDATE: mc showed sizes in "KiB" indeed, that was one of the reasons for different file sizes I noticed.
But there was another reason: Syncthing kept some *.tmp files on device B which made the total size of the folders bigger.

Sorry about these chaotic updates - as mentioned, I have to get these files in sync. So I just synced them between A and C with Resilio and re-ran Syncthing.
Although all files were in sync and total size of the folders was the same Syncthing showed some files as "out of sync" on device C. So I just deleted them manually on C and re-ran the sync and finally got Syncthing to understand that this folder was in sync on A and C.

And now this folder is in an interesting state from Syncthing point of view: the UI says this folder is in sync between A and B and also between A and C, but it's "out of sync" between B and C.

UPDATE: I was able to get it all in sync after restarting Syncthing on device B.

While there's no mentioning of crashes/panics/unclean shutdowns in the comments, the missing indexes still make it likely that the underlying problem is https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing/issues/6335, which has been fixed (but not yet released). Please report if you still experience this with >= 1.4.0-rc.5.

@calmh I added it to the 1.4.0 milestone - is that enough for changelogs?
After upgrading syncthing to the fixed version the problem might still persist and then can be finally fixed by running `syncthing -reset-database`.
